uterus.description: In the pelvis, behind the bladder and in front of the rectum. The cervix joins its lower end to the vagina.
uterus.function: Supports pregnancy; its muscular wall contracts during birth.
uterus.clinicalNotes: After childbirth, assess fundal firmness, position and bleeding according to your clinical protocol.

cervix_of_uterus.description: The lower neck of the uterus projects into the upper vagina.
cervix_of_uterus.function: Its canal connects the uterine cavity and vagina.
cervix_of_uterus.clinicalNotes: Relate cervical screening and reported bleeding to this site; explain examinations and obtain consent.

vagina.description: A canal behind the bladder, in front of the rectum, extending down from the cervix.
vagina.function: Provides a passage for menstrual flow and childbirth.
vagina.clinicalNotes: Distinguish the vaginal opening from the urethral opening when learning urinary catheter landmarks.

ovary_l.description: Beside the uterus, close to the open end of the uterine tube.
ovary_l.function: Releases oocytes and produces ovarian hormones.
ovary_l.clinicalNotes: Document pelvic pain and its side; sudden severe pain needs prompt assessment.

uterine_tube_left.description: Extends from the upper uterus toward the ovary; its fringed end opens nearby.
uterine_tube_left.function: Transports the oocyte toward the uterus; fertilization usually occurs in its ampulla.
uterine_tube_left.clinicalNotes: Use these landmarks to understand why a pregnancy outside the uterus needs assessment.

breast_left.description: On the front of the chest; glandular tissue drains through ducts toward the nipple.
breast_left.clinicalNotes: When assessing breastfeeding, check comfort, nipple condition and latch.
